intent: 28 candidates against the four measured deficits rather than against a percentage. THREE LAMB and FOUR SEAFOOD-OR-FISH, because lamb is 4 recipes of 201 and seafood is 4. SEVEN at five core lines or fewer, because honest short recipes are 29 against a ~44 target. Two breakfast/street snacks, because breakfast is 37 against 145 lunches. Nineteen are Egyptian, which is the natural consequence of going after those deficits rather than the aim: not one of these is a foreign dish relabelled, and `shorbet-2ar3` was just reclassified OUT of Egyptian in the same stage for exactly that reason. Fourteen candidates exist partly to use catalogue rows no recipe touches: lamb-chops, lamb-shank, crab, lupini-beans, artichoke, purslane, chard, turnip, roqaq, barley, ricotta, sumac, coconut-milk, dried-apricot. Nothing already tried is in the pool.

candidates.name: Grilled Lamb Chops
candidates.note: Four lamb recipes in 201, and the lamb-chops row has none. Five minutes a side over real heat.

candidates.name: Braised Lamb Shank
candidates.note: Friday lunch, a cheap cut and almost no work. The lamb-shank row is unused. A veal shank was tried in batch 4 and got osso buco; this is a different cut, a different search and a different dish.

candidates.name: Crab in Tomato and Garlic
candidates.note: Alexandria in summer. The crab row is used by nothing at all.

candidates.name: Prawns in Tomato Sauce
candidates.note: Distinct from the garlic-butter pan of prawns already here: this one is a sauce you eat with rice or bread.

candidates.name: Fried Bolti
candidates.note: The fish Egypt actually eats, floured and deep fried. Grilled mullet and sayadeya are both in the catalogue; fried bolti is neither.

candidates.name: Lupini Beans
candidates.note: Four lines, no cooking beyond a long soak, and the lupini row has no recipe. Street food you eat out of a paper cone.

candidates.name: Hot Chickpeas with Cumin
candidates.note: Boiled chickpeas in their own broth with cumin and lemon. Winter street food, five lines, and nothing like the hummus dip already here.

candidates.name: Boiled Eggs with Cumin and Salt
candidates.note: Three lines. Breakfast is 37 recipes against 145 lunches, and this is what half of Egypt eats on the way to work.

candidates.name: Fried Cauliflower
candidates.note: Five lines. The roasted cauliflower with tahini in the catalogue is a different dish in every respect but the vegetable.

candidates.name: Artichokes in Oil and Lemon
candidates.note: Spring, and the artichoke row has no recipe.

candidates.name: Purslane with Garlic
candidates.note: Rural Egyptian green, five lines, and the purslane row is unused. Photography is the risk here, not the recipe.

candidates.name: Chard and Lentils
candidates.note: The chard row has no recipe. A thick pot rather than a soup, which is what separates it from the four lentil soups already here.

candidates.name: Turnips with Beef
candidates.note: Winter stew, and the turnip row is used by nothing.

candidates.name: Braised Cabbage with Beef
candidates.note: Not the stuffed cabbage already in the catalogue — this is cabbage braised down with beef until it goes sweet.

candidates.name: Spinach with Beef
candidates.note: One of the handful of stews on rotation in most Egyptian houses.

candidates.name: Grilled Beef Kebab
candidates.note: Chunks on a skewer, not mince. Five lines. Grilled kofta was searched for in batch 4 and found nothing; this is a different dish and a different search.

candidates.name: Stuffed Roast Chicken
candidates.note: The festive version of the bird already in the catalogue: stuffed with spiced rice rather than rubbed with cumin.

candidates.name: Roqaq Pie with Minced Beef
candidates.note: Eid food. Layers of dried roqaq sheets soaked in milk and butter over spiced mince, and the roqaq row has no recipe.

candidates.name: Kofta Baked in Tahini
candidates.note: The third kofta in the catalogue and genuinely the third dish: the tagine is tomato and potato, the salsa is a stovetop tomato sauce, this one bakes under tahini.

candidates.name: Beef Shawarma
candidates.note: Chicken shawarma is here; beef is the other half of every shawarma counter and a different marinade.

candidates.name: Sumac Chicken with Onions
candidates.note: A kilo of onions, sumac and bread underneath to catch the juices. Nothing in the catalogue uses sumac as the main seasoning.

candidates.name: Lamb Curry
candidates.note: Lamb again, from the other direction, and genuinely cooked in Egyptian homes.

candidates.name: Fish Curry
candidates.note: Fish is 11 of 201 recipes. This one is a sauce rather than a grill or a bake.

candidates.name: Lamb Tagine with Apricots
candidates.note: Third lamb candidate on purpose. Sweet-savoury, slow, and it uses the dried-apricot row for something other than a compote.

candidates.name: Prawn and Garlic Pasta
candidates.note: Seafood and a weeknight pasta at the same time. The garlic prawns already here are a pan dish with no pasta in them.

candidates.name: Spinach and Ricotta Pasta
candidates.note: A substantial vegetarian main that is not a legume, and the ricotta row is unused.

candidates.name: Baked Fish with Potatoes
candidates.note: One tray, fish and its side together. Distinct from the sayadeya rice and from the grilled bream.

candidates.name: Barley and Vegetable Soup
candidates.note: Cheap, filling, keeps for days, and the barley row has no recipe.
